# Getting Rid of Time: Solving for t

<!-- STEP id="why-bother" -->
Some problems tell you u, a and s, but not t — a braking car's stopping *distance*, say, without caring how many seconds it took. For those, a formula linking v, u, a and s directly — with no t in it at all — would be far more useful.

<!-- STEP id="start-again-from-eq1" -->
Start from the first equation:

$$v = u + at$$

<!-- STEP id="isolate-t" -->
Subtract u from both sides, then divide both sides by a:

$$v - u = at \quad\Rightarrow\quad t = \frac{v - u}{a}$$

<!-- STEP id="ready-to-substitute" -->
Now t is written purely in terms of v, u and a — with no t on the right-hand side. That's exactly what's needed to remove t from the second equation next.
